document.abstract: This paper introduces the core concepts associated with the modern integration of the software systems used in media facilities. The principles of service-oriented architecture (SOA) and associated technologies are described in an introductory and accessible form. This paper also provides a tutorial on the basics of cloud technology. Public and private clouds, Software as a Service (SaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS), and other related topics are covered. Advantages and disadvantages in taking a cloud-based approach is examined. The application of these technologies in the media industry is interlaced throughout the paper.

authors.bio: John Footen is an acknowledged industry expert in such areas as Business Process Management (BPM), Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA), and the Cloud, all of which have a major impact on today's broadcast television and professional media systems. As head of Cognizant's broadcast consulting practice, Footen is responsible for business and technology consulting throughout the broadcast industry. Footen is a sought-after speaker and expert writer on software architecture and workflow issues. He serves as co-chair of the Framework for Interoperable Media Services (FIMS) joint taskforce of the Advanced Media Workflow Association (AMWA) and European Broadcasting Union (EBU). Footen is a SMPTE member and chairs the 34CS Media Systems Control and Services technology committee. He has been responsible for managing many large and complex media solutions projects for many types of media enterprises. He has extensive international experience; having lived and worked in North America, Asia, and Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA). Footen holds degrees in computer science and film and television from New York University. He is also the co-author of “The Service-Oriented Media Enterprise: SOA, BPM, and Web Services in Professional Media Systems,” published by Focal Press.
authors.name: John Footen

authors.bio: Mohan Ananthanarayanan has extensive experience in information technology, SOA, BPM and the Enterprise Application Integration (EAI) space. Ananthanarayanan's experience includes consulting, IT presales, solution architecture, systems analysis, technical design and development, spanning multiple Industry domains. His areas of specialization include IBM Websphere suite of products and he has been involved in architecture assessment and product evaluation exercises for multiple clients. At Cognizant, Ananthanarayanan is a principal architect focusing on IBM Websphere suite of products and is part of the Integration Consulting Group which oversees complex integration projects under EAI practice. In his current role Ananthanarayanan leads the IBM Business Process & Integration practice within Cognizant responsible for business development and consulting.
